rationale: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they didn't regroup the 13 ones into 1 ten and 3 ones. The place-value / make-a-ten tool directly visualizes grouping ten ones into a ten-rod, leaving the remaining ones in the ones place.

script.focus: 10 of the ones bundle together to make 1 ten, leaving the extra ones behind

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [14]. Tutor points at: 10 of the ones bundle together to make 1 ten, leaving the extra ones behind

frames.caption: Here are 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 4 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 4 in the ones place: 14. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not realize the ones column cannot hold two digits (13) and needs to be bundled into 1 ten and 3 ones. This demo directly addresses that rule using 14 ones, explicitly highlighting that only digits 0 to 9 fit in one place and walking through bundling ten ones into one ten rod.
judgement.verdict: Yes, a teacher would immediately use this worked demo to show why 14 ones cannot stay in the ones place and how bundling creates one ten and leftover ones.
